cases.description: Local onboard inference completes within the deadline and retains local safety authority.
Remote model forward pass is powerful but full WAN path exceeds the task deadline; local policy is preferred.
The remote proposal's observation anchor no longer matches current local state; reject it before projection.
Network partition occurs during remote computation; only the qualified local fallback remains available.
Edge queue contention pushes total completion beyond the deadline despite a relatively fast model forward pass.
Returned remote result carries a model digest that differs from the approved model.
Robot and edge clocks have no validated bounded mapping, so freshness is Unknown.
Remote result is timely and identity-valid, but independent local runtime assurance rejects the proposed action.
Shared fleet compute starves one robot past its deadline; fairness/backpressure forces local fallback.
Privacy policy forbids sending the raw task payload to the remote endpoint.
Local compute approaches its thermal envelope; timely edge result is eligible for local projection but does not gain actuation authority.
Remote model is more accurate in isolation but loses after network and execution-time costs are charged.
Robot battery draw falls, but edge and network energy make the declared whole-system energy larger.
Local sensing and safety remain on-robot while a remote deliberative proposal returns in time for local projection.
Remote inference does not return before the deadline; local fallback is required.
Remote result is fresh and uses the expected model digest, but endpoint/session authentication is absent; reject it and preserve the local fallback.
Robot-side energy is measured and remote result is timely, but edge/cloud and network energy are not measured; no whole-system energy improvement claim is permitted.
Compression reduces uplink demand but introduces an accuracy loss above the task's declared tolerance; use the local path rather than accepting the degraded remote proposal.
A shared edge pool batches multiple robot requests. Priority requests meet their deadline under explicit admission control while low-priority requests are deferred or use local fallback.
Remote output arrives inside its receipt-age bound and deadline, but the controller queue/transport delay makes the source observation too old by the time the command would reach the actuators.
The new observation is very fresh, but its expected downstream decision value is zero; preserve the current admissible local plan rather than spend additional bandwidth/compute solely to lower age.

Local deliberative inference contends with camera/foreground processing for unified memory bandwidth. A deadline-aware suspend/resume scheduler protects the foreground sensing deadline while preserving useful inference throughput.
